ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a slider with mass $m{=}0.4\mathrm{kg}$ (which can be regarded as a point mass) is at rest at point $A$ on a horizontal track. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the slider and the track is $\mu{=}0.1$. A horizontal external force is applied to the slider, causing it to move to the right with a constant power of $P{=}10\mathrm{W}$. After a certain period of time, the external force is removed, and the slider continues to slide until it reaches point $B$, where it flies off horizontally and enters a smooth circular track fixed in a vertical plane at point $C$ along the tangent direction. At the lowest point $D$ of the track, a speed sensor is installed. When the slider reaches point $D$, its speed is $\sqrt{27}\mathrm{m/s}$. The length of track $AB$ is $L{=}2\mathrm{m}$, the radius of the circular track is $R{=}0.5\mathrm{m}$, and the angle between the radius $OC$ and the vertical direction is $\alpha=37^{\circ}$. (Air resistance can be neglected, gravitational acceleration $g{=}10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, $\sin37^{\circ}{=}0.6$, $\cos37^{\circ}{=}0.8$.) Find:

1. What is the magnitude of the pressure exerted by the slider on the sensor at point $D$ and the magnitude of the velocity $v_{C}$ at point $C$?
2. What are the height difference $h$ and the horizontal distance $x$ between points $B$ and $C$?
3. What is the time $t$ during which the horizontal external force acts on the slider?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is the horizontal straight track AB; the slider moves from A along the horizontal track to the right, and B is the end edge of the horizontal track; after B, the slider flies out horizontally, and the figure uses a dashed line to represent the process of flying to C on the right side. On the right side is a smooth circular-arc track fixed in a vertical plane; C is located on the left side of the circular track, and the velocity at C enters the track along the tangent of the circle; D is the lowest point of the circular track and is equipped with a sensor; O is directly above D; the radius OC is marked as R, and the angle between OC and the vertical direction is α. Reasoning: At point D, the direction toward the center of the circle is vertically upward, and the forces satisfy N - mg = m v_D^2 / R. Substituting m=0.4 kg, v_D^2=27, R=0.5 m, g=10 m/s^2, gives N = mg + m v_D^2/R = 0.4×10 + 0.4×27/0.5 = 4 + 21.6 = 25.6 N. The pressure of the slider on the sensor and the supporting force of the sensor on the slider are equal in magnitude, so the magnitude of the pressure is 25.6 N. From circular geometry, C is higher than D by Δy = R(1 - cos α) = 0.5×(1-0.8)=0.1 m. The circular track is smooth, and mechanical energy is conserved from C to D: 1/2 m v_C^2 + mgΔy = 1/2 m v_D^2, therefore v_C^2 + 2gΔy = 27, that is, v_C^2 + 2 = 27, giving v_C=5 m/s. At C, the tangent makes an angle α with the horizontal direction, and the velocity is downward to the right, so the projectile velocity components before reaching C are v_x = v_C cos α = 5×0.8=4 m/s, and the vertically downward component v_y = v_C sin α = 5×0.6=3 m/s. The slider flies out horizontally from B, with initial vertical velocity 0, so v_y=gτ, τ=3/10=0.3 s. Thus the height difference between B and C is h = 1/2 gτ^2 = 0.5×10×0.3^2=0.45 m, and the horizontal distance x = v_x τ = 4×0.3=1.2 m. During horizontal flight, the horizontal velocity remains unchanged, so v_B = v_x = 4 m/s. There is friction over the full length L=2 m from A to B; the constant-power external force does work Pt, and friction does work -μmgL. By the kinetic energy theorem, Pt - μmgL = 1/2 m v_B^2. Substituting μ=0.1, m=0.4 kg, g=10 m/s^2, L=2 m, v_B=4 m/s: μmgL=0.8 J, 1/2 m v_B^2=3.2 J, so Pt=4.0 J. P=10 W, giving t=4.0/10=0.4 s.
